title: Choose the board's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Drafting Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Drafting Sheet
options.lineage: architects' construction drawings and their revision markup
options.thesis: The repository drawn as a construction sheet; your plan is the redline on it.
options.viewport: A full-bleed sheet: fine non-photo-blue grid with lettered and numbered border references, layers drawn as levels with level markers at the left, packages as plan outlines, the title block bottom-right holding repo, branch and rule status, and every planned move marked in red pencil with a numbered delta.
options.risk: Becomes blueprint costume (white lines on blue) if the drawing conventions are decoration rather than how the board works.

raised.raise: The Run log and the violation list are a fixed-column ledger whose rows restyle by state without breaking the grid.
Current and planned layouts share one scale and registration, so a toggle compares before and after in place.
Layer bands are flat fields that do the dividing on their own; no boxed group borders.
Card weight follows one fixed ramp of lines of code, so the biggest modules read first.
Cards snap to the sheet's grid modules, and snapping is a visible state.

options.label: Transit Schematic
options.thesis: Layers as lines and packages as stations; dependencies are the routes between them.
options.viewport: A white schematic with each layer as a coloured line, packages as stations along it, and interchange rings where layers depend on each other.
options.risk: The most familiar metaphor for dependency tools, and schematic routing strains past a few hundred edges.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Every module a row on a live departures board.
options.viewport: Ruled rows of modules ranked by size, status lamps for violations.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a board of rows cannot show the shape of a dependency graph, the first thing people need.
options.risk: A dark, tabular board fights the canvas the product depends on.
options.kept: Fixed-column ledger rhythm for the Run log and violations.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Modules as stars sized by magnitude on one chart.
options.viewport: A dark chart with modules as dots sized by lines of code.
options.case: Fuses partly: size-as-magnitude is clear, but a night chart drifts toward the dark look you ruled out and developers don't read the metaphor.
options.risk: Reads as the dark 'hacker' board with better manners.
options.kept: A fixed size ramp carries hierarchy.

options.label: Crouwel Grid
options.thesis: A visible construction grid every card is built on.
options.viewport: A white sheet with a visible grid and monumental type.
options.case: Fuses partly: the grid suits the board, but its monumental type costs canvas and says nothing about dependencies.
options.risk: Poster type eats the space the graph needs.
options.kept: Snap to whole grid modules as a visible state.

options.label: Guide-map Lobes
options.thesis: Layers as flat colour territories with coastlines.
options.viewport: Layers as swelling coloured lobes; modules as labelled points on them.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful territories undercut a tool that gates real code changes.
options.risk: Whimsy where precision is the promise.
options.kept: Flat fields divide on their own, no boxes.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Before and after as plates at one fixed scale.
options.viewport: Current and planned layouts as matched plates side by side.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an engraved, cream world says nothing to developers about code.
options.kept: Registration: compare states at one scale.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: Package names in coarse pixel type over dense columns.
options.case: Fuses poorly: retro type styling, no help reading a graph.
options.risk: Novelty that wears off by the second session.
options.kept: Labels step between a few fixed sizes per zoom level.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A whiteboard-style graph canvas, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A light canvas of rounded cards in tinted group regions with a floating toolbar and inspector.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every diagram and graph tool by design.

outcome: user steered to established software-architecture notation (canon); combined layered + C4 + UML + DSM
